issues.description: Function 'check_status': the problem statement requires check_status to return a Boolean value (0 or 1) in EAX. The template repository does not provide an implementation (students must implement it). The solution repository implements check_status as 'mov eax, hello' which places the address of the 'hello' data label into EAX (a pointer), not a Boolean 0/1. This mismatch will cause the implemented/solution check to disagree with the specification and may cause automated validation or student expectations to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution's check_status to return an explicit Boolean in EAX (0 or 1) instead of the address. For example replace 'mov eax, hello' with 'mov eax, 1' (or implement the intended check logic and ensure it sets EAX to 0 or 1). Also clarify in the problem statement or template the expected symbol/signature for check_status so students implement the correct behavior.

issues.description: The assembly register identifier is inconsistent across artifacts: the template uses the invalid register name 'ecc' in the instruction 'add eax, ecc' (template_repository/helloWorld.asm line 13), the problem statement instructs students to change 'ecc' to 'ecx' (problem_statement.md line 17), and the solution uses 'ecx' in 'add eax, ecx' (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm line 16). Students cannot compile the template as-is and will be blocked or confused mapping the problem requirement to the template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the incorrect register identifier 'ecc' with the correct register 'ecx' in the template file (change 'add eax, ecc' to 'add eax, ecx' in template_repository/helloWorld.asm) so the template, problem statement, and solution consistently reference the same CPU register.
